note: Code derivation: data/mexico_2023_quality.py (#2415 rebuild) lowercases INEGI column names and melts P5_1_01..P5_1_12 (core model s3 pattern 1 for 2023: code IS the INEGI 2023 column name). Step 3b / what 'low' is: the dictionary Description 'Low Demand Services' is a mistranslation of INEGI's section title 'Seccion V. Evaluacion de servicios publicos BAJO DEMANDA' (= on-demand public services, i.e. services a person uses by choice, as opposed to section IV's basic services). The live items are NOT quality ratings: they are question 5.1, the section-V USE SCREENER ('Digame si durante 2023 en (ESTADO), ¿usted... fue usuario(a) de ...?', Si/No) whose Si answers route the respondent into 5.2-5.13 (the sibling _schooling, _university, _health, _wellbeing, _healthservice, _wellbeingservice, _homelightning, _buses, _transportationstations, _cablecars, _trains, _highways tables). No instrument mismatch with the data -- 12 live items = 5.1's 12 options -- but the Description should read something like 'Use of on-demand public services (ENCIG 5.1 screener)'. 2021 rows: ENCIG 2021's 5.1 had 10 options (no IMSS-Bienestar, no Cablebus/Mexicable); RENAME_2021 maps P5_1_1..5 -> p5_1_01..05, P5_1_6 -> p5_1_07, P5_1_7 -> p5_1_08, P5_1_8 -> p5_1_09, P5_1_9 -> p5_1_11, P5_1_10 -> p5_1_12; p5_1_06 and p5_1_10 carry 2023 rows only. 2021 wording differs only in 'durante 2021', ungendered forms (usuario, alguno de sus hijos) and '(Sólo en las ciudades que aplica)' where 2023 prints '(Solo en los estados que aplica)'. Code->text: the questionnaire numbers 5.1's options 01-12, matching the variable names; INEGI's zip carries no data dictionary, so mapping_basis=paper_explicit, not data_labels. Verified (verify_mexico_2023_quality_low.R, PASS): route 9 per wave 12/12 (2023) and 10/10 (2021) item vectors reproduce INEGI microdata cell for cell, each matching only its mapped P5_1 column; and a per-person routing check -- for every item, the set of Si respondents equals exactly the set who answered the follow-up block 5.1 routes it to (APLICA 5.x Y 5.xa) and no other block, in both waves -- ties each column to the content of its follow-up question. Resp: the .py recodes 1 (Si) -> 0, 2 (No) -> 1 and sets 9/98/99 missing (5.1 prints no code 9), so resp 0 = Si, 1 = No; both levels used by every item. Text: 2023 wording shipped verbatim (15/15 Spanish strings exact substrings of pdftotext p.7, whitespace/dot-leaders normalised; checked against the rendered page image). Stem -> section_prompt of the single section (the '…' is printed); options -> item_text; item 01 begins 'o alguno(a)...' because it continues the stem '¿usted…'. Kept as printed: fills (ESTADO)/(TRANSPORTE) and the applicability notes '(Solo en los estados que aplica)' (items 09, 11) and '[CDMX y EDO. MEX.]' (item 10), which are interviewer-facing but explain the structural missingness of those items (2023 blank for 22724/32475/31609 of 38966). Stripped: option numbers, dot leaders (incl. the '...' after item 06, a leader in the page image), interviewer directions (REGISTRA EL CODIGO CORRESPONDIENTE A CADA OPCION; CON CODIGO 2 PASA AL SIGUIENTE SERVICIO; CON CODIGO 1: APLICA 5.x Y 5.xa; EN CASO DE QUE EN TODAS LAS OPCIONES SE REGISTRE CODIGO 2, PASA A LA SECCION VI). instructions blank (the section-V read-aloud C3 block is not carried, as in the sibling tables). English (_translated) is this project's own translation (machine_translation); INEGI publishes no English questionnaire. Sheet1 STOP overridden, Ben to confirm: table_context.R printed STOP (Sheet1 links a hand-built per-table sheet 1oYRN7BPVDyqknh8O3p7zaH_zujarOpGP_45lc7u6owg); proceeded, as batch_424's _health did, because the orchestrator queued it under #2381, the table is not in live_tables.csv (never uploaded), and that sheet fails the gate as-is (resp 1/2 vs live 0/1 -- its NOTES say it deliberately kept the codebook's 1/2; option numbers '01 '.. prefixed into item_text; trailing '?.' on items 06 and 09).
